A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bayes-assisted, anytime-valid PPI framework. Their full main texts and appendices, including equations, proofs, figures and tables, support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original noisy- and biased-prediction simulations and experiments on Flights, Forest and Galaxies, measuring interval volume and cumulative miscoverage.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds multivariate simulations, regression and median-estimation experiments, predictor-performance measurements, and a preprocessing study.

M1.justification: The core PPI/PPI++ estimators and Bayes-assisted construction remain. However, the multivariate confidence-region formula changes from t/(2pi) in v1 Sections S5.2–S5.3 to t^d/(2pi)^d in v2 Sections S4.2–S4.3, correcting the reported radius for d greater than one.

E1.justification: V2 retains the three original mean-estimation datasets and adds Census linear regression, Healthcare logistic regression, and Genes median estimation. It also evaluates five-dimensional mean estimation, substantially expanding coverage beyond v1's scalar-mean experiments.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the classical, PPI/PPI++, and Gaussian, Laplace and Student-t prior comparisons. The improper-prior alternative already appeared in v1 Section S9. Added tasks reuse existing comparison methods or subsets of them.

E3.justification: The biased-prediction simulation changes noise scale from 10 to 1, bias range from [-5, 5] to [-1.2, 1.2], and default t-star from 100 to 500. New experiments introduce filtering, logarithmic preprocessing, pilot-centered parameter grids, task-specific monitoring starts, and multivariate radius evaluation.

E4.justification: V2 adds multivariate prior-bias sensitivity analysis in Figure S9 and a substantive preprocessing check in Figure S12. The latter exposes a nominal-coverage violation without Census preprocessing. Existing scalar bias, prior-scale and improper-prior analyses are retained, with revised biased-simulation evidence.

E5.justification: V1 Figures S6–S7 report 100 repetitions; corresponding v2 Figures S7–S8 report 1000. This establishes changed repetition-count reporting, but v2 Figure 2 still states 100 for results also displayed in Figure S7, leaving the actual count for shared panels inconsistent.

E6.justification: V2 adds predictor scores, multivariate radii, and regression/median results. Figure S11 shows Bayes-assisted PPI++ producing wider intervals on Genes; Figure S12 shows non-assisted PPI++ exceeding 0.1 cumulative miscoverage without Census preprocessing. Figure 2's results also change under revised simulation settings, so they do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: V2 introduces a little-o approximation-rate definition and Theorem 5 with a proof of asymptotic time-uniform Type-I error control. It adds explicit variance-estimation rates and scalar prior-support conditions and corrects multivariate normalization. KMT coupling and multivariate extensions already existed in v1's appendices; their relocation alone is not new theory.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains sequential, Bayes-assisted PPI. V2 explicitly qualifies the abstract and introductory coverage claim as asymptotic and acknowledges the existing multivariate extension in its discussion, refining the scope and precision of the headline claims.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands practical qualifications: it explains how preprocessing and monitoring start times affect coverage, attributes unsuccessful Bayes assistance on Genes to prediction bias, and discusses conservative multivariate regions. Section S6.3 also distinguishes predictive accuracy from task-dependent rectifier quality, while the discussion adds computational and delayed-start considerations.

D1.justification: V2 adds a Python implementation repository link, detailed preprocessing and grid-initialization instructions, and the previously unspecified Student-t prior degrees of freedom of 2. It reports Apple M4 Pro hardware with 24GB memory instead of the Intel i7-11850H and explicitly states the already-used parameter-free alternative's formula.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting sequential error control, prediction applications, Genes data and the proposed Berry–Esseen guidance, while dropping Strassen and Kallenberg references. It refines the description of Csillag et al.'s assumptions from bounded outcomes to bounded e-values. The overall positioning relative to PPI and confidence-sequence research remains similar.

P1.justification: V2 consolidates v1's separate stronger-rate development into the main theory and reorganized proofs, restructures the background and experimental appendices, and rewrites the discussion and alternative-CS exposition. It also adds a confidence-interval versus confidence-sequence explanation and an appendix contents list.

P2.justification: V2 adopts NeurIPS typography and page layout, changes figure placement, and redraws the biased-prediction plots with revised axes. It adds the CI/CS illustration, multivariate and additional-task plots, the preprocessing comparison, and predictor-performance Table S1. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 strengthens the inferential justification through explicit regularity conditions, mathematical corrections and an error-control proof. Its broader experiments also reveal practical failures rather than only successful scalar-mean examples, and implementation information improves reproducibility. These substantial gains outweigh remaining duplicated reference numbers and inconsistent repetition-count captions.
